strategy.summary: ICT's fair value gap on its own: a fast displacement bar leaves a three-candle gap, price comes back into it, and (ICT says) continues. A placebo study found real FVGs no better than random zones, and a random walk reproduces the famous fill rates, so every setting runs twice: with the gap (ICT) and against it (the control). Rank 4 of the ICT research survey (reports/ICT strategies to backtest.md).
strategy.formula: 3-bar gap after a displacement bar → with: buy the retrace into a bullish gap (limit); against: sell the same retrace (stop order)

rules.label: ATR
rules.text: 14-bar mean of 1-minute true range at the gap's first bar, before the displacement. It warms up on the overnight bars.

rules.label: Gap
rules.text: Three consecutive 1-minute bars all opening inside the window, with high[1] < low[3] (bullish) or low[1] > high[3] (bearish). The gap must be at least 0 or 0.5 ATR and the middle bar's range at least 1, 1.5, 2 or 3 ATR. Optional VWAP gate: the trade's direction must agree with bar 3's close vs the session VWAP (from 09:30).

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: With: a limit at the gap's near edge or midpoint (needs a 1-tick trade-through). Against: a stop order at the same level (fills on a touch, with stop slippage). Or market at the next bar's open. Orders rest 5, 15 or 30 bars inside the window. One trade a session.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Stop beyond the three bars' extreme (+2 ticks) or 1.5 / 3 ATR away, never closer than 1 ATR, checked first within a bar. Target 1R, 2R, 3R or none (a limit needing a 1-tick trade-through, not on the fill bar). Otherwise out after 15, 30 or 60 minutes, and always by 16:00.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Never held overnight. As many whole NQ contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

strategy.length_note: Times are New York clock times. ATR warms up on the Globex bars from 18:00; trading uses 09:45–16:00 ET.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 24,192 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the 1-minute ATR, the session VWAP and every three-bar gap were recomputed from the raw bars with plain loops; each trade's gap, window, side, fill (limit, stop order or market), stop, target and exit were re-derived; fills were never better than the market; one trade a session; nothing held past 16:00. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 756 (756 on 1min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 23,350 (23,350 on 1min); 19,757 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: the displacement by ±0.25 ATR, the gap minimum by ±0.25 ATR, the order life by ±5 bars, an ATR stop by ±0.5, an R target by ±0.5R and the hold by ±5 minutes (structural stops, market entries and no-target versions have nothing to nudge on those settings). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 3.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 83 versions formed 29 groups; 52 of the 52 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

luck.method: Per finalist: the same window, fill kind, stop rule, target and hold, and as many trades, but each on a random validation-window session at a random bar in the window, long or short by a fair coin. Same fills, slippage, commission and whole-contract sizing as the strategy; scored with the same daily-Sharpe and time-in-market code.
luck.text: For each finalist, 500 random runs on 2023–2024 make the same number of trades with the same window, fill type (limit, stop order or market), stop rule, target and hold, but each on a random day at a random minute, long or short by a coin flip. So they test whether the gap itself (when to trade and which way) beats chance. They pay the same costs and use the same sizing and Sharpe math as the strategy. The chart groups finalists by window, with each finalist's random runs at its own time in market (0.1% steps).

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (NQ.v.0), 1-minute Globex bars from 18:00 the evening before to 16:00 ET. Rolls are back-adjusted; positions never cross a session.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side and $2.50 commission per contract per side. Limit fills need a 1-tick trade-through; stop orders pay slippage.

ICT definitions vary between teachers; these rules are one mechanical reading fixed before the run. The report's 216-cell grid was widened to 24,192 before any run, which makes the deflated-Sharpe correction larger.

With vs against: if gaps carry no information, both modes lose about the costs. Across the whole grid 23% of 'with' versions were profitable (median PF 0.92) against 8.5% of 'against' (median PF 0.84).
Each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the other families.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of 1-minute bars with an open position.
Other strategy families were already selected on this market's 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is.
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
